description: Analysing linear electric circuits from Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws through nodal and mesh analysis, network theorems, first- and second-order transients, sinusoidal steady state with phasors and AC power, ending with diodes and transistors as circuit elements. Every circuit is built and measured on a simulated bench in the browser, with virtual meters and an oscilloscope checking each hand calculation.
modelledOn: Alexander and Sadiku, Fundamentals of Electric Circuits
Hayt, Kemmerly and Durbin, Engineering Circuit Analysis
Sedra and Smith, Microelectronic Circuits (introductory chapters)
outcomes: Apply Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's laws and the passive sign convention to compute voltage, current, power and energy in resistive circuits.
Solve any linear circuit, including dependent sources and ideal op-amps, by nodal and mesh analysis in matrix form.
Simplify networks with superposition, source transformation and Thevenin and Norton equivalents, and design for maximum power transfer.
Derive and sketch the transient response of first- and second-order RC, RL and RLC circuits after switching.
Analyse circuits in sinusoidal steady state with phasors and impedance, and calculate real, reactive and complex power and power-factor correction.
Model diodes and transistors as circuit elements and design simple rectifier, regulator and switching circuits.

units.title: Circuit variables and elements
topics: Charge, current, voltage, power and energy; the passive sign convention
Ideal independent and dependent (controlled) voltage and current sources
Resistance, Ohm's law, conductance and resistivity; open and short circuits
Power ratings and energy in kWh; reading a prepaid electricity meter and estimating a household bill
Measuring with ammeters, voltmeters and ohmmeters; meter loading errors

units.title: Kirchhoff's laws and resistive circuits
topics: Nodes, branches, loops and meshes; Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws
Series and parallel resistors; voltage and current division
Wye-delta transformations and bridge networks; the Wheatstone bridge
Equivalent resistance by inspection and by test source
Worked circuits: torch, charger and household lighting circuits

units.title: Nodal and mesh analysis
topics: Node-voltage method; supernodes for voltage sources between nodes
Mesh-current method; supermeshes for current sources shared by meshes
Circuits with dependent sources; writing the equations in matrix form
Solving the systems by Gaussian elimination and Cramer's rule; checking with the simulator
Choosing between nodal and mesh analysis
The ideal operational amplifier as a circuit element: inverting, non-inverting, summing and difference amplifiers

units.title: Network theorems
topics: Linearity and the superposition principle
Source transformation between voltage and current sources
Thevenin and Norton equivalents, including circuits with dependent sources
Maximum power transfer and its efficiency cost
Modelling a solar panel, battery and inverter as Thevenin sources for an off-grid home

units.title: Capacitors, inductors and first-order transients
topics: Capacitor and inductor voltage-current relations, stored energy and continuity conditions; series and parallel combinations
Source-free RC and RL circuits; the time constant
Step response of RC and RL circuits; initial and final values by inspection
Singularity functions: unit step, impulse and ramp
Switching transients and inrush current when power returns after a power cut
First-order op-amp circuits: integrator and differentiator

units.title: Second-order circuits
topics: Source-free series and parallel RLC circuits; the characteristic equation
Overdamped, critically damped and underdamped responses; damping ratio and natural frequency
Step response of RLC circuits and finding initial conditions
General second-order circuits and duality
Ringing and overshoot observed on the simulated oscilloscope

units.title: Sinusoids, phasors and impedance
topics: Sinusoids: amplitude, frequency, phase and RMS value; the 230 V, 50 Hz national grid supply
Complex numbers and phasors; phasor relations for R, L and C
Impedance and admittance; series and parallel impedance combinations
Kirchhoff's laws, nodal and mesh analysis in the frequency domain
Thevenin and Norton equivalents, and superposition with sources of different frequencies
Phasor diagrams and AC measurements

units.title: Power in AC circuits
topics: Instantaneous and average power; effective (RMS) values
Apparent, reactive and complex power; the power triangle
Power factor and power-factor correction with capacitors; why utilities penalise poor power factor
Maximum average power transfer
Balanced three-phase systems in brief: wye and delta connections, line and phase quantities, three-phase power
Domestic wiring, earthing, fuses and circuit breakers; electrical safety

units.title: Frequency response, resonance and coupled circuits
topics: Transfer functions and frequency response; Bode plots in brief
Series and parallel resonance; quality factor and bandwidth
Passive low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and band-stop filters
Mutual inductance and the ideal transformer; step-down transformers in chargers and distribution

units.title: Diodes and transistors as circuit elements
topics: The pn-junction diode: I-V characteristic; ideal, constant-voltage-drop and piecewise-linear models
Half-wave and full-wave rectifiers; smoothing capacitors and ripple voltage
Zener diodes and simple voltage regulators; LEDs and current-limiting resistors
The bipolar junction transistor: regions of operation, DC biasing and the load line; the BJT as a switch and as a small-signal amplifier
The MOSFET as a switch for driving loads
Capstone: design and test a mains-to-5 V phone charger on the simulated bench

schedule.title: Circuit variables, sources and measurement
schedule.exercise: Solve a problem set on power and energy sign conventions, and estimate a month of prepaid electricity cost for a household from appliance ratings and hours of use.

tasks.title: Build a series circuit with a 12 V source and a 470 ohm resistor, predict the current with Ohm's law and confirm it on the simulated meter
Measure a 10 kilohm divider output with a voltmeter of 100 kilohm input resistance and calculate the percentage loading error against the unloaded value
Build a circuit with a current-controlled voltage source, find the gain that makes the output power exactly 1 W, and verify by sweeping the gain

schedule.title: Kirchhoff's laws and resistive networks
schedule.exercise: Reduce three resistor networks to a single equivalent resistance by hand, showing each series, parallel and delta-wye step, and verify one numerically.

tasks.title: Build a voltage divider from two resistors for a 3.3 V output from a 12 V supply and verify the output and each branch current
Balance a Wheatstone bridge using a variable resistor until the detector reads zero and compute the unknown resistance from the ratio
Diagnose a lighting circuit with one dead branch by comparing node voltages to hand-calculated values and identify the open resistor

schedule.title: Nodal and mesh analysis
schedule.exercise: Write the node-voltage and mesh-current equations for three given circuits, including one with a dependent source, and solve each by hand.

tasks.title: Write node equations for a three-node resistor circuit, solve them as a 2 by 2 system and check the node voltages on the circuit bench
Solve a two-mesh circuit with a shared current source using a supermesh and confirm the mesh currents by measurement
Set up the conductance matrix for a four-node circuit with a voltage-controlled current source, solve it and compare with the bench result

schedule.title: Solving systems and operational amplifiers
schedule.exercise: Solve a 3 by 3 circuit system using both Gaussian elimination and Cramer's rule, then decide in writing which analysis method suits two further circuits.

tasks.title: Solve a 3 by 3 mesh system with Cramer's rule in the maths lab and check each determinant and mesh current against the circuit simulation
Build an inverting amplifier with a gain of minus 10 and verify the output for three input voltages, noting where the output saturates
Design a summing amplifier that mixes three sensor voltages with weights 1, 2 and 4 and verify the output for four input combinations

schedule.title: Network theorems and sources
schedule.exercise: Find the Thevenin equivalent of a bridge circuit and a circuit with a dependent source by hand, then state when superposition cannot be applied directly.

tasks.title: Apply superposition to a two-source circuit by turning each source off in turn, add the partial currents and confirm the total on the bench
Measure the open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current of a network, derive its Thevenin equivalent and show the load current matches the original
Model a solar panel and battery as Thevenin sources, find the load resistance giving maximum power and report the efficiency at that point

schedule.title: Capacitors, inductors and first-order circuits
schedule.exercise: Derive the time constant and voltage equation for an RC charging circuit and use it to compute how long a capacitor takes to reach 99 percent of the supply.

tasks.title: Discharge a 100 microfarad capacitor through a 10 kilohm resistor, read the voltage after one time constant and compare it with 36.8 percent
Record the step response of an RL circuit on the simulated oscilloscope and extract the time constant graphically from the 63.2 percent point
Plot capacitor voltage and stored energy for an RC circuit with several resistor values and determine which value stores most energy at 2 ms

schedule.title: Singularity functions, transients and op-amp circuits
schedule.exercise: Write the response of an RC circuit to a pulse of finite width using step functions, and sketch the waveform with the time constants marked.

tasks.title: Plot a unit step, a ramp and a pulse made from two shifted steps in the maths lab and verify the pulse area numerically
Simulate switching on a capacitive load after a power cut and read the peak inrush current, then add a series resistor to limit it to 5 A
Build an op-amp integrator, feed it a square wave, and check the output is a triangle wave with the amplitude predicted by the component values

schedule.title: Second-order circuits
schedule.exercise: Classify five RLC circuits as overdamped, critically damped or underdamped from their component values, and compute damping ratio and natural frequency for each.

tasks.title: Compute the roots of the characteristic equation for a series RLC circuit and state whether the response is over, under or critically damped
Vary the resistance in a series RLC circuit until the response is critically damped and record the value that stops oscillation
Measure percentage overshoot and ringing frequency of an underdamped step response on the oscilloscope and compare with the damping ratio from theory

schedule.title: Sinusoids, phasors and impedance
schedule.exercise: Convert six sinusoids between time-domain and phasor form, and compute the impedance of series and parallel RLC combinations at 50 Hz.

tasks.title: Measure the amplitude, frequency, phase and RMS value of a 230 V, 50 Hz sinusoid on the simulated oscilloscope and check the RMS equals peak over root two
Add three sinusoids of the same frequency by converting them to phasors in the maths lab and plot the sum against the time-domain waveform
Find the impedance of a series R-L-C branch at 50 Hz, predict the current phase angle and verify the measured phase shift on the bench

schedule.title: AC circuit analysis and measurements
schedule.exercise: Solve a two-mesh AC circuit with complex arithmetic, draw its phasor diagram to scale and state which element dominates the phase angle.

tasks.title: Draw the phasor diagram of an RL series circuit from measured voltages and check that the resistor and inductor voltages add at 90 degrees
Write and solve the nodal equations of a two-node AC circuit with complex numbers and compare node voltage magnitudes with the simulator
Find the Thevenin impedance of an AC network and use superposition to compute the output when two sources at 50 Hz and 150 Hz act together

schedule.title: AC power and electrical safety
schedule.exercise: Compute power triangle quantities for a workshop load, size the capacitor that corrects its power factor to 0.95 and estimate the saving on the utility bill.

tasks.title: Measure real, reactive and apparent power of an inductive load and check that apparent power equals the square root of the sum of squares
Add a parallel capacitor to a 0.7 power factor motor load and raise the factor to 0.95, then verify the line current falls as predicted
Compute line and phase currents and total power for a balanced three-phase load in wye and delta and compare the two connections for the same supply

schedule.title: Frequency response, resonance and transformers
schedule.exercise: Derive the cut-off frequency of an RC low-pass filter and the bandwidth of a series resonant circuit, then explain how a phone charger transformer steps mains voltage down.

tasks.title: Build an RC low-pass filter with a 1 kHz cut-off, sweep the input frequency and mark the minus 3 dB point on the response plot
Tune a series RLC circuit to resonate at 10 kHz and measure its quality factor and bandwidth from the half-power points
Plot the Bode magnitude and phase of a second-order band-pass filter and design component values for a given centre frequency and bandwidth

schedule.title: Diodes, transistors and the phone charger capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a design report for a mains-to-5 V phone charger that gives the circuit diagram, component values, expected ripple, and a list of safety checks.

tasks.title: Build a full-wave bridge rectifier with a smoothing capacitor and measure the ripple voltage for two capacitor values against the formula
Bias a BJT to drive a small relay as a switch, choose the base resistor and show the transistor reaches saturation when the input goes high
Design and test a transformer, rectifier, capacitor and Zener regulator chain delivering 5 V at 500 mA, and report ripple, regulation and power dissipated
